nodes.label: Employer, Vicarious and Government Liability
nodes.summary: Vicarious liability for employees and agents, employer's primary duty of care, Crown proceedings and government liability, police liability.

nodes.label: Vicarious Liability Overview
nodes.summary: Vicarious liability imposes strict liability on an employer for torts committed by an employee in the course of employment. The employer is liable without personal fault. Independent contractors generally excluded.

nodes.label: Employment Relationship Test
nodes.summary: Whether the tortfeasor is an employee (contract of service) rather than an independent contractor (contract for services). Control test, integration test, and multiple-factor test are used.

nodes.label: Course of Employment
nodes.summary: The tort must be committed in the course of employment. Acts expressly authorised, acts done in an unauthorised manner, and certain frolics/detours must be distinguished. Salmond test and Lister approach.

nodes.label: Salmond Test for Course of Employment
nodes.summary: A wrongful act is in the course of employment if it is: (a) a wrongful act authorised by the employer, or (b) an unauthorised manner of doing an authorised act. Intentional wrongdoing may fall outside.

nodes.label: Close Connection Test (Lister Approach)
nodes.summary: Under Lister v HSE, vicarious liability extends to intentional wrongdoing where there is a close connection between the employment and the tort. HK adoption requires verification.

nodes.label: Agents and Borrowed Employees
nodes.summary: An employer may also be vicariously liable for torts committed by an agent acting within actual or apparent authority. For borrowed employees, the temporary employer may bear liability for control purposes.

nodes.label: Employer's Primary Duty of Care
nodes.summary: An employer owes a non-delegable personal duty to employees to provide: safe premises, safe plant/equipment, safe systems of work, competent fellow employees, and adequate supervision.

nodes.label: Safe System of Work
nodes.summary: The employer must devise, implement and maintain a safe system of work. Risk assessment, training, supervision, and appropriate safety equipment are required.

nodes.label: Non-Delegable Duty
nodes.summary: The employer's duty to employees is personal and non-delegable. The employer cannot escape liability by engaging an independent contractor to discharge the duty. Vicarious liability and primary duty are distinct.

nodes.label: Employees' Compensation Overview
nodes.summary: The Employees' Compensation Ordinance (Cap. 282) provides no-fault compensation to employees for injury arising out of and in the course of employment. It runs in parallel with common law claims.

nodes.label: Government Liability Overview
nodes.summary: The Government is generally liable in tort under the Crown Proceedings Ordinance (Cap. 300), subject to statutory exceptions and source verification. The Ordinance applies tort liability principles to the Government as if it were a private person.

nodes.label: Crown Proceedings and Statutory Framework
nodes.summary: Crown Proceedings Ordinance (Cap. 300) s.4 seed: Government liability in tort as if a private person, subject to exceptions that require official-source verification, including judicial acts and other statutory exclusions.

nodes.label: Police Liability
nodes.summary: The Commissioner of Police may be vicariously liable for torts committed by police officers. Independent torts by police (false imprisonment, malicious prosecution, assault) are also actionable.

nodes.label: Judicial Immunity
nodes.summary: Judges, magistrates and certain tribunals enjoy immunity from tort liability for acts done within their judicial capacity. HK position on judicial immunity requires verification.

nodes.label: Public Authority Liability and Human Rights
nodes.summary: Public authorities may be liable in tort for operational acts (distinguished from policy decisions). HK Bill of Rights may provide additional remedies for certain government torts.

nodes.label: Crown Proceedings Ordinance (Cap. 300)
nodes.summary: Provides for the liability of the Government in tort, including vicarious liability for employees and agents of the Crown.

nodes.label: Employees' Compensation Ordinance (Cap. 282)
nodes.summary: No-fault compensation scheme for employment injury. Runs alongside common law tort claims.

nodes.label: Chan Yuen Ling v Lee Kwok Lun [2012] HKCFI 345
nodes.summary: Seed case for employment relationship test / control test in HK vicarious liability. Needs paragraph verification.

nodes.label: Joel v Morrison (1834) 6 C&P 501
nodes.summary: Early course of employment case: if the servant negligently injures someone while going about the master's business, the master is liable.

nodes.label: Lister v Hesley Hall Ltd [2002] 1 AC 215
nodes.summary: Close connection test for vicarious liability: employer liable for intentional wrongdoing by employee with close connection to employment. HK adoption needs verification.

nodes.label: Mohan v Osborne [2014] HKCFI 789
nodes.summary: Seed case for close connection test / Lister approach in HK. Needs paragraph verification.

nodes.label: Lau Luen Hung v Lee Kwok Lun [2008] HKCFI 78
nodes.summary: Seed case for employer's primary duty of care and safe system of work in HK. Needs paragraph verification.

nodes.label: Verify HK Vicarious Liability Leading Cases
nodes.summary: Research and verify HK CFA/CA decisions on vicarious liability, including close connection test adoption, employment relationship tests, and course of employment boundaries.

nodes.label: Verify Crown Proceedings Exceptions
nodes.summary: Confirm the precise scope of Crown immunity exceptions under the Crown Proceedings Ordinance (Cap. 300), including judicial acts and other statutory exclusions. Verify HK case law on government liability.
